    plots show a summary of the marks for the assessments for two
    students, Jamie and Maryanne.

![](media/Data Analysis A 2_Quartiles and Box Plots/media/image53.png){width="3.34375in"
height="1.6736111111111112in"}

a.  Who scored the highest mark?

Jamie

b.  Who scored the lowest mark?

Jamie

c.  What was the range of marks for each student?

Jamie: 55, Maryanne: 30

d.  Who had the greater spread of marks?

Jamie

e.  What was the interquartile range for each student?

Jamie: 25, Maryanne: 20

f.  Whose marks were the more consistent?

Maryanne, smaller range and IQR

g.  Who had more marks over 70?

Jamie had 50% compared to 25% for Maryanne.

    height="1.7291666666666667in"}A new Toyota Corolla and Mazda 3 were
    each taken for ten test drives over the same routes. These parallel
    box plots show a summary of the fuel consumption, in L/100 km, of
    each vehicle

    a.  Which car recorded the highest fuel consumption?

Corolla

b.  Which car recorded the lowest fuel consumption?

Corolla

c.  Which car had the greater range of results?

Corolla

d.  Which car demonstrated the more consistent fuel consumption over all
    routes?

> Give a reason.

Mazda 3, smaller IQR

e.  Which car used less than 7 L/100 km more often?

Corolla was less than 7L/100 km \<50% of the time. Mazda 3 was less than
7L/100 km \> 50% of the time. So Mazda.

5.  **2016 HSC Standard 2 Band 4\**
    The box-and-whisker plots show the results of a History test and a
    Geography test.

 In History, 112 students completed the test. The number of students who
scored above 30 marks was the same for the History test and the
Geography test.

![](media/Data Analysis A 2_Quartiles and Box Plots/media/image58.png){width="3.37in"
height="1.9979188538932633in"} How many students completed the Geography
test?

![](media/Data Analysis A 2_Quartiles and Box Plots/media/image59.png){width="0.7463768591426072in"
height="1.3143405511811024in"}

For the History test, $30$ represents the upper quartile ($Q_{3}$). This
means $25\%$ of the History students scored above $30$.\
\
$${\begin{matrix}
\text{Number of History students above }30 & = 0.25 \times 112 \\
 & = 28
\end{matrix}
}
$$We are told this number ($28$) is the same for Geography.\
For the Geography test, $30$ represents the median ($Q_{2}$),
meaning $50\%$ of the Geography students scored above $30$.\
\
$$\begin{matrix}
50\%\text{ of Geography students} & = 28 \\
\text{Total Geography students} & = 28 \times 2 \\
 & = 56
\end{matrix}
$$**C**

6.  ![](media/Data Analysis A 2_Quartiles and Box Plots/media/image60.png){width="3.30625in"
    height="1.7361964129483816in"}**2005 HSC Standard 2 Band 6**\
    Two groups of people were surveyed about their weekly wages. The
    results are shown in the box-and-whisker plots.

Which of the following statements is true for the people surveyed?

![](media/Data Analysis A 2_Quartiles and Box Plots/media/image61.png){width="6.223053368328959in"
height="1.331288276465442in"}

\- Option A: For \"People under 21 years\", $325$ is the median
($50\%$ earned more). For \"People 21 years and older\", $325$ is the
lower quartile ($75\%$ earned more). This is false.\
- Option B: For \"People under 21 years\", $350$ is the upper quartile
($Q_{3}$). This means $75\%$ of this group earned less than $\$ 350$.
This is true.\
- Option C: For \"People 21 years and older\", $350$ is the upper
quartile. This means $25\%$ earned more than $\$ 350$, not $75\%$. This
is false.\
- Option D: For \"People under 21 years\", the
range $\$ 325$ to $\$ 350$ is from $Q_{2}$ to $Q_{3}$ ($25\%$ of the
group). This is false.\
\
Therefore, Option B is the only true statement.
